answer: By imposing quadratic slashing on dispersed staking collateral, the protocol forces adversaries to sink liquidity into a high-entropy lantern of verifiable identity, effectively elevating the marginal cost of network subversion beyond the extraction horizon. Because individual participation costs scale super-linearly with cluster size, any malicious actor attempting to reach the summit of consensus control incurs a capital expenditure exceeding projected utility. This robust Nash equilibrium renders sybil attacks prohibitively expensive.
